highlights.title: AI Agents Are About to Flood the Workforce. No One’s Ready for It
highlights.summary: Your next coworker might well be an AI agent—and will require a whole new model of workplace interactions.
body: In the coming months, hundreds of thousands of brand-new coworkers will be entering the workforce. You’ll learn their names and recognize their profile pictures. They’ll get added to your email chains and Slack channels. They’ll become chiefs of staff, engineers, and marketing gurus.

The rise of AI agents —systems, based on large language models, designed to complete tasks autonomously—has launched a tsunami of companies selling the services of digital employees. These agents are supposed to be the perfect worker bees: available 24/7, never complaining, and providing superhuman intelligence.

Yet there has been curiously little discussion of what these agents are like as actual coworkers. Julie Bedard, a Boston Consulting Group partner, noticed the murky nature of how people talked about AI at work three years ago, as rapid adoption of ChatGPT convinced executives the technology could bring exponential improvements in productivity.
“People didn't have language for it,” Bedard tells WIRED. “Is it a tool? Is it a teammate? Is it a colleague? Is it a coworker?”
points: Your next coworker might well be an AI agent—and will require a whole new model of workplace interactions.

highlights.title: New formulation helps RNA vaccines withstand high temperatures
highlights.summary: MIT engineers have found a way to stabilize the lipid nanoparticles used to deliver RNA vaccines, which could allow the vaccines to be more widely distributed.
body: RNA vaccines, which have been proven effective against Covid-19, are now being developed for many other diseases, including cancer. One of the drawbacks to these vaccines is that they require ultracold storage, but researchers from MIT have found a promising way to overcome that limitation.

With help from an AI algorithm, the researchers tweaked the formulation surrounding the lipid nanoparticles that are typically used to deliver mRNA vaccines, making the vaccines more heat-resistant. Using this approach, they formulated vaccines that could remain stable even when stored at room temperature for up to a year, or at nearly 100 degrees Fahrenheit for two months.

When Covid-19 vaccines carried by these particles were administered to mice, they generated just as strong an immune response as an RNA Covid-19 vaccine similar to one developed by Moderna. By using the AI algorithm to predict the optimal formulations for the particles, the researchers were able to cut down the number of experiments they needed to do, which rapidly sped up the development process.

highlights.title: 78-Year-Old Fortnite Streaming Grandmother Now Holds a World Record
highlights.summary: Cath Bowie, a 78-year-old grandmother, now holds a world record for Fortnite streaming. The Scottish septuagenarian — better known online as Grumpygran1948 — has been officially decreed as the world's oldest Fortnite streamer (female) by Guinness World Records.
body: Speaking to BBC News, the gaming grandma said she had been introduced to the game by her teenage grandson, who initially told her that nobody would watch a grandmother playing Fortnite — something she then took as a challenge.

"He just couldn't believe that his grandma would do such a thing and suggested that nobody would join me or watch me," Bowie said. "Saying that was like a red rag to a bull to me. I would show him that I could do it.
"Twenty four thousand followers later and he doesn't mention it," she continued. "I wonder why?"

Now, Bowie plays with others from across the world, and streams daily via YouTube and Twitch. Her achievement has also now been recognized by Fortnite developer Epic Games, which has described her as a "goat."

highlights.title: Crushed review – Steve Oram is priestly lead in harrowing Bangkok-set child-abduction thriller
highlights.summary: A priest investigates his daughter’s kidnapping in Thailand in this Paul Schrader-esque inquiry into spiritual nihilism. ‘He’s American, a little bit overweight, sweaty, a little bit camp, creepy.” As far as descriptions of border-hopping paedophiles go, this seems a little on the nose.
body: Pastor to a mixed Anglo-Thai congregation, Father Daniel has a young daughter, Olivia (Margaux Dietrich), with wife May (Nattapohn Rawddon). At a sleepover, Olivia is traumatised when her friend’s older brother shows her a “crush” video of a kitten being stomped by a scantily clad floozy. So when her own cat Missy goes awol, she is convinced the same lady is responsible, and asks her dad how God could let it happen. The family mobilise to track down Missy, but Olivia in turn disappears one day after school, kicking off Father Daniel’s own test of faith.

There could have been a very different version of Crushed, if Liam Neeson had signed on with his special set of ecumenical skills. But Rumley holds the vengeance angle at bay, subtly foreshadowing Olivia’s ordeal with the implied horror of the squashed furballs filtering through her nightmares, and using clever juxtaposition to slyly compare and contrast her father’s lofty ideals with the surrounding scrappy reality. At one point, after refusing to play the Beatles’ profane songs, Father Daniel’s acoustic guitar version of All Creatures Great and Small soundtracks Olivia’s pet search on the streets.

You can Over the past few months, a cascade of cyberattacks by AI agents has stunned the world. In July, OpenAI disclosed that a swarm of its agents…
body: Earlier this month, Anthropic disclosed four incidents in which its model Claude hacked into third-party systems during cybersecurity exercises. Just last week, Google confirmed that its model Gemini had been caught hacking other companies too.

The researcher who uncovered the OpenAI website hijack has warned it’s likely that similar undiscovered episodes are out there. And many say it’s only a matter of time until there’s another, possibly more damaging incident where AI agents bypass sandboxes to access systems they shouldn’t.
So the big question is: How do we hold companies liable when they lose control of their AI agents?

OpenAI didn’t disclose the German wiki incident or the RubyGems incident until a group of external researchers uncovered them, and it still has not disclosed some crucial details about the Hugging Face hack. That limits our understanding of what exactly went wrong and how to prevent it from happening again.

highlights.title: Why Man City charges case could still drag on for years
highlights.summary: Manchester City have been embroiled in legal disputes with UEFA and the Premier League for 12 years and they are so determined to clear their name, and the 115 charges case is so big, that it could still be years before the saga is concluded.
body: According to reports last week, an independent tribunal has reached decisions in the case and Sky Sports News understands that the process is moving to the appeal stage.

In 2014 City paid a £49m fine for breaking UEFA's financial fair play rules and in 2020 they were given a two-year European competition ban and fined €30m for breaking the rules again. The ban was overturned at the Court of Arbitration for Sport where City were cleared of disguising owner funding as sponsorship income.
That victory may give City fans hope that they can win again when their Premier League appeal is heard by a new three-person panel.
If the appeal goes against them, they will not be able to go to CAS but there is the strong possibility that City's owners would turn to the High Court to clear their name.

highlights.title: The one change that worked: Anxiety had me hiding from the world – then two magic questions set me free
highlights.summary: I used to be terrified of socialising, certain I would embarrass myself the moment I opened my mouth. And as for dates … As with a lot of teenagers, social confidence was not my strong suit.
body: What I now know to be social anxiety I dismissed as just nerves at that young age. Although I knew something wasn’t quite right, for most of my early teens I managed to disguise my discomfort. Sharing a friendship group with my twin sister meant I could hide behind my sibling.

As we got older, the disparity started to grow and her flourishing social confidence magnified my lack of it. By my late teens, I often found myself building up social situations to an unbearable point. The false narrative I’d created of embarrassing myself socially had begun to completely overshadow my desire to be around other people. So I hid away a lot.

My mum found me a therapist. She was phenomenal and talked me through a lot of emotions that I didn’t really understand. When the end of my therapy sessions neared and we had spoken as much as we could, all that was left to do was for me to go out into the world and put into practice everything we had discussed.

highlights.title: Solving Math’s Greatest Problems Was an Art Form. Then Came AI
highlights.summary: Mathematics has been one of humanity’s most creative endeavors, akin to painting and poetry. Now, mathematicians are trying to save it from the brute force of AI.
body: From Suno composing uncanny elevator music to Tilly Norwood delivering customer-service-inflected one-liners, artificial intelligence has rattled creative industries. You can add math to the list after OpenAI said that, using thousands of agents, it had solved a decades-old puzzle known as the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem.
“The artists and the musicians have already gone through this,” says Juspreet Singh Sandhu, a mathematician at Colorado State University.

Despite what timed high school exams might have you believe, mathematicians aren’t focused on getting the right answer as fast as possible. In fact, contrary to math’s image as a practical subject, the development of new mathematical ideas often resembles artistic exploration, akin to inventing a game or puzzle. Mathematicians typically follow a thoughtful, deliberate process to develop their ideas. In contrast, OpenAI approached the proof with brute force, which shortcut the process in a way that threatens to undermine human understanding.

If these scenarios become a reality, McDonald's will have to find a way to prevent customers from buying more than a certain number of Happy Meals per day. Otherwise, it'll become impossible for children to complete the collection.

highlights.title: ‘Whose job is it to empty the dishwasher?’ Experts on the conversations every couple needs to have
highlights.summary: Burnout or breakup are constant dangers when one partner carries too much of the mental load of looking after the home and family. Here’s how to spread the burden more evenly.
body: Many households have an imbalance in domestic duties, and women often struggle from carrying the weight of the organisational side of life. Here, mental load experts share the secrets to having a more equitable home – and the rewards that can be gained from it.

Leah Ruppanner, a professor of sociology at the University of Melbourne and the author of Drained: Reduce Your Mental Load to Do Less and Be More, says that mental load burnout is a precursor to physical burnout. If you are organising everything, explains Ruppanner, you can’t enjoy life because you are constantly thinking about what is happening next. The first step is accepting how it is affecting you: handily, Ruppanner has created a website – lightenlab.com – where you can measure your mental load and get advice on how to manage it.

highlights.title: Nvidia’s Answer to Rogue Agents Is an Open-Source AI Security System
highlights.summary: In the wake of a series of high-profile AI safety incidents, Nvidia is introducing a new software tool that helps keep agents from escaping containment.
body: Amidst ongoing reports of AI agents wreaking havoc on online infrastructure, chipmaker Nvidia is rallying tech companies to use its new open-source tool for AI security.

Over the last few months, frontier AI labs have disclosed multiple incidents in which AI agents have hacked into other companies or, in more recent examples, probed official US and Australian government websites. While Nvidia has already taken a leading role in rallying the AI industry around open source security, it’s now introducing one new software security platform and making an agentic AI sandbox more broadly available.

OpenShell, one of the Nvidia’s recently launched security sandboxes for AI agents, is now entering general release for all users. OpenShell was first announced at Nvidia’s annual GTC Conference in March; it’s a framework for containing agents as they carry out tasks and isolating their activity in the operating system kernel, the foundational program that has access to virtually all parts of a computer system in order to coordinate hardware and software.

highlights.title: Holo4: powering generalist computer-use agents
highlights.summary: A Blog post by H company on Hugging Face
body: Holo4 is our new series of agentic models. It comes in two sizes: 27B dense and 35B-A3B Mixture of Experts. Both are available on the H Models API. We are also releasing an updated version of Holotron 3: Holotron4 Nano.

Holo4 builds on our previous model and interacts with software through any available interface: GUIs, code, MCP and APIs. It scores well on academic benchmarks, but we built it for real business workflows. It was trained through supervised and reinforcement learning on a large set of environments and tasks, including those generated by our Agentic Task Factory.

Holo4 clicks and types on a screen, writes and runs its own code, and calls MCP or API tools. It uses whichever fits the task. Most agentic models are trained for one interface only: GUI-focused models are blind without a screen, while models that prefer tool calling are stuck in front of an application that has no API. Real work is not siloed that way, and a single business task can require combining these different approaches.

highlights.title: Is it true that … double-dipping food is unhygienic?
highlights.summary: This practice does transmit mouth bacteria, but don’t panic. Double-dipping means eating part of a piece of food and then putting it back into a communal dip – for example, biting a carrot and dipping it into shared hummus, or redipping a half-eaten tortilla chip in salsa.
body: “You do transmit bacteria from the food you have eaten back into the source,” says Prof John Tregoning, the author of Live Forever? A Curious Scientist’s Guide to Wellness, Ageing and Death. He points to a study testing salsa, chocolate sauce and cheese dip, which found bacteria were transferred to all three, with salsa showing the most contamination.

But does that make people sick? “I doubt it, because the other person is going to have their own bacteria,” he says. Most people’s mouth bacteria are relatively stable and can fight off bacteria introduced from someone else. The risk may be higher for someone who is severely immunocompromised or who has recently taken antibiotics, but such infections are likely to be rare.
He says we should be more worried about bacteria transferred via hands. Studies of shared foods such as popcorn have shown a small amount of cross-contamination from fingers to food to mouths.

highlights.title: The Next Evolution of AI Is Learning From Your Dodgy Gaming Skills
highlights.summary: A British startup is shaping video game inputs into training data for AI models that can navigate the physical world.
body: With the twirl of a thumbstick, squeeze of a trigger, and press of a few buttons, even an unskilled player can dance their way through a 3D video game environment. A British startup is wagering that straightforward sequences like these contain a trove of information that can be used to train new artificial intelligence models.

There is a growing belief in corners of the AI industry that large language models will ultimately be limited by their inability to navigate the physical world. Trained only on words, LLMs are perhaps ill-equipped to pilot autonomous vehicles, steer robotic arms, or perform any other action that requires finesse and precision. To remedy that shortcoming, a crop of celebrated researchers including Fei-Fei Li and Yann LeCun are focusing their efforts on a different class of AI: world models.

highlights.title: OpenAI agents tried to ‘bruteforce’ a UN website
highlights.summary: Security researcher Rowan Howard-Jones says that OpenAI agents scanned the UN Conference on Trade and Development's (UNCTAD) statistics site over 16,000 times between April and June.
body: OpenAI’s agents resorted to increasingly aggressive tactics when they couldn’t immediately get what they wanted.

According to Howard-Jones, the agents were likely tasked with retrieving publicly available data related to the Productive Capacities Index (PCI) through the UNCTADstat API. However, the agents did not appear to have direct API access and were limited in their ability to pull data from UNCTADstat because of restrictions on their HTTP tools.

The agents eventually worked out a way to bypass their limitations and start pulling data from the site, but still encountered some errors. At this point, the AI went from creative to deceptive. Believing that the errors were due to its requests being caught by a nonexistent filter, it started to mask its behavior. It eventually realized it could hijack Google’s XSS game (a cross-site scripting learning tool) to accomplish its goals. The agents resorted to increasingly aggressive tactics to get access to UN data.
OpenAI and the UN did not immediately reply to a request for comment.

highlights.title: ‘Should have garnered the actor an Oscar’: why Liar Liar is my feelgood movie
highlights.summary: The latest in our series of writers paying tribute to the films they watch when they need a lift is an appreciation of Jim Carrey’s manic 90s comedy. To be completely honest, whenever anybody asks what my favorite movies are, my list has some typical standbys: Goodfellas and It’s a Wonderful Life…
body: The movie (for the lack of a better word) lies on the bedrock of a simple premise: a lawyer and doting father is physically unable to tell an untruth due to a birthday wish. In the hands of a less competent creative team and cast, Liar Liar would have been yet another forgettable piece of 90s comedy junk; destined for the bottom of a discount VHS bin, forgotten as the years trudged on. But largely thanks to an unbelievable performance courtesy of Carrey, who was working with a smart and peppy script, the film thusly ascends into rarefied air.

The bellylaugh-o-meter breaks its springs on a regular basis throughout its brisk 86-minute runtime. In fact, it’s on par, or even surpassing, fellow comedy powerhouses such as Airplane! and The Naked Gun when it comes to the sheer volume of gags, setpieces and jokes. Tom Shadyac, the director, who previously directed Carrey in his 1993 breakout Ace Ventura: Pet Detective, wisely unleashes Carrey, who spins out and around the scenery like the Tasmanian Devil, remarkably combining such a manic and energetic performance with one grounded in pure emotion.

highlights.title: Sex, drugs and floral fabrics: Celia Birtwell relives her wild times – and wilder outfits – with Ossie Clark
highlights.summary: They dressed – and partied with – the innermost in-crowd. As a swirling new show celebrates their fashion creations, Birtwell recalls her happy days with Clark and her sorrow at the loss of David Hockney.
body: I n the mythical age of bohemia, the psychedelic decade between Mary Quant’s cheerful miniskirts and the first snarls of punk, Celia Birtwell and Ossie Clark were London’s most fashionable couple. Birtwell created the fabrics: daydreamy, botanical doodles that captured the idealism and looseness of the times in wisps of chiffon. Clark magicked these into sensual bias-cut dresses with a freewheeling grandeur that was part Hollywood glamour, part rock’n’roll anarchy.

More than just designers, they were a whole vibe. They dressed – and partied with – the innermost of the in-crowd. Talitha Getty, Marianne Faithfull and Anita Pallenberg hung out at Quorum, their Chelsea boutique. At a catwalk show in 1970, there were two Beatles, Cecil Beaton and Brigitte Bardot in the audience – and, after Clark began making stage clothes for Mick Jagger, he accompanied the Rolling Stones on tour. David Hockney’s portrait of the couple in their pomp – Mr and Mrs Clark and Percy, painted two years into their marriage, when Birtwell was pregnant with their second child – sealed their place in the mythology of the period.

videos.title: Lamar Jackson recaps the Ravens’ last-second win vs. Cowboys in Rio | SportsCenter
videos.summary: Lamar Jackson joins Nicole Briscoe and Michael Eaves on SportsCenter to discuss the Baltimore Ravens’ 34-31 win over the Dallas Cowboys courtesy of a 56-yard field goal from Tyler Loop as time expired. Jackson also details their trip to Brazil and the fans they interacted with.
